title: fix: declare and enforce transcription endpoints
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Declares `/v1/audio/transcriptions` for `whisper`, `scribe`, `universal-2`, and `universal-3.5-pro` in the shared registry.
- Makes `/models`, `/audio/models`, and `/v1/models` report the same endpoint data.
- Enforces the transcription endpoint during model resolution, so invalid TTS/music model IDs return 400 before reaching a provider.
- Removes the `requireTextToAudioModel` guard: registry enforcement now rejects every model it could catch, making it dead code.
- Preserves valid routes, providers, aliases, access, pricing, and billing.

Behavior changes:
- STT models on `/audio/{text}` and `/v1/audio/speech` still 400, but the error message format changes to `Model "x" cannot be used on <endpoint>. Supported endpoints: ...`.
- STT model IDs on the music endpoint now 400 at model resolution (`available only on: /v1/audio/transcriptions`) instead of reaching the handler.

Tests:
- `npx vitest run test/index.test.ts` (50 passed)
- Audio VCR tests (passed)
- Gen typecheck and Biome (passed)

gist.headline: The audio garden has fences
gist.blurb: The audio registry now knows which flowers belong in the transcription bed. Send a music model to speech-to-text and it gets a clear little signpost before wandering into a provider.
gist.summary: Declared `/v1/audio/transcriptions` for Whisper, Scribe, Universal-2, and Universal-3.5-Pro in the shared audio registry, unified endpoint reporting across `/models`, `/audio/models`, and `/v1/models`, and enforced endpoint compatibility during model resolution.
gist.impact: Developers now get consistent model metadata and an immediate 400 explaining supported endpoints when a TTS, music, or transcription model is used on the wrong audio route.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy audio garden with clearly labeled paths for transcription, speech, and music models: Polli acts as a gentle park ranger, placing a sign that directs microphone-shaped transcription flowers to the correct `/v1/audio/transcriptions` plot while keeping a misplaced music-note seedling from entering it. A CRT monitor robot can display matching endpoint listings, representing the three model-listing endpoints now agreeing.
gist.image_prompt: In a cozy pixel-art audio garden, Polli—the cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body, dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular cheek blushes, a small happy smile, and small rounded light-blue translucent wings—wears a tiny ranger hat and points a microphone-shaped flower toward a sign reading `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, while a cute CRT monitor robot shows matching model lists and music-note seedlings follow their own path. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft lime green (#ecf874) and pastel gradient background, code-plants and flowers, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes, nostalgic but beautiful.
